whatFailed: DELETE /api/tcref-not-a-content-type/<documentId>, a path no content-type declares, answers 405 Method Not Allowed with Allow: HEAD, GET and a plain-text body, while GET on the exact same path in the same run answers 404 with Strapi's JSON error envelope.

docClaim.quote: | `DELETE` | `/api/:pluralApiId/:documentId` | [Delete a document](#delete) |  ...  **Parameters:** - `pluralApiId` (string, required): Plural API ID (e.g. `restaurants`) - `documentId` (string, required): Document ID of the entry to delete  ...  Requests return a response as an object which usually includes the following keys: ... `error` (object, _optional_): information about any [error](/cms/error-handling) thrown by the request
docClaim.section: rest-api-reference/endpoints + rest-api-reference/requests/delete-a-document-delete (upstream: https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest, source lives in the separate strapi/documentation repo)

observed: server.stdout.txt: 'DELETE /api/tcref-not-a-content-type/kd5glmt3qd4fro8k5967nx8h (1 ms) 405'; response body is the bare string 'Method Not Allowed' (response.txt / response.raw.txt), i.e. Koa's default status text, not JSON. In the same run (read-one-document-by-its-documentid.api.1, step 5) 'GET /api/tcref-not-a-content-type/oxu7drtrrz6081a4c0mcn43n' returned 404 with {"data":null,"error":{"status":404,"name":"NotFoundError","message":"Not Found","details":{}}}. So the same non-existent resource is reported as absent to GET and as existing-but-wrong-method to DELETE.
impact: Any integrator who mistypes a pluralApiId (or calls a content-type whose route was disabled) gets a misleading 405 with Allow: HEAD, GET, telling them the URL is right and the verb is wrong, when GET on that URL is a 404 too; the body is plain text rather than the documented JSON error envelope, so generic Strapi error handling (response.json() / reading error.status) breaks. Applies to every non-GET/HEAD method on every unrouted path in every Strapi app, not just the content API.

rootCause.explanation: The strapi::public middleware registers a GET route whose path is the catch-all regexp '/((?!uploads/).+)' on the shared top-level Koa router so koa-static can serve ./public. packages/core/core/src/services/server/index.ts:79 mounts that router as app.use(router.routes()).use(router.allowedMethods()). @koa/router 12.0.2 (pinned in packages/core/core/package.json:62) builds allowedMethods from ctx.matched, which is matched.path: every layer whose PATH regexp matched, regardless of whether its handler ran (@koa/router lib/router.js:479-531, read from the published 12.0.2 tarball). The public catch-all matches every path except /uploads/..., and its Layer methods are ['HEAD','GET'] (lib/layer.js:27-29 unshifts HEAD for GET). So for a request with no route at all, allowed = {HEAD, GET}, the request method DELETE is not in it, and allowedMethods sets ctx.status = 405 with Allow: HEAD, GET. Setting the status explicitly also flips Koa's ctx.response._explicitStatus, which makes the strapi::errors middleware skip its ctx.notFound() fallback (packages/core/core/src/middlewares/errors.ts:16-19) - that fallback is exactly what produces the JSON {data:null,error:{status:404,...}} envelope the GET on the same path gets. Result: 405 plus a plain-text body instead of 404 plus the documented envelope. Middleware order is confirmed by packages/core/core/src/services/server/register-middlewares.ts:7-18, where strapi::errors is registered before strapi::public and before the router mount. Secondary sites: packages/core/core/src/services/server/index.ts:79 and packages/core/core/src/middlewares/errors.ts:16-19.

colleagueFinding.note: None of the researcher's 8 Strapi findings covers this. Theirs are MCP-tool, admin-token, filter-operator, page-size, SQL-leak and docs items; this one is the core REST router answering 405 rather than 404 for unrouted paths, and it is not MCP related.

notes: Two caveats a maintainer should hear. (1) The bound doc never states a status code for an unknown pluralApiId; it only lists 'pluralApiId (string, required)' and shows a 404 example under Get a document. The scenario turned 'required' into 'expect 404', which is an inference, so the specific expected value was over-specified. What makes this still a product defect rather than a test defect is the product's own inconsistency, visible in the same run: GET on that exact path returns 404 with the documented {data,error} envelope, DELETE returns 405 with Allow: HEAD, GET and a plain-text body, and the docs' Requests section does promise an 'error' object for errors. The Allow header is factually wrong: GET on that path is also a 404. (2) Step 4 of this scenario (DELETE /api/articles, documentId omitted, expect 404) never ran because step 3 aborted the scenario, but it would also have failed with 405 - and there 405 is the CORRECT answer, since /api/articles is a real resource supporting GET, HEAD and POST. If this scenario is regenerated, step 4's expectation should become 405 with Allow containing GET and POST, and step 3's should become 404 with the JSON error envelope. Suggested upstream fix: register the koa-static handler as plain app-level middleware (or via router.all / a method-agnostic layer) instead of a GET router route, so an unrouted path does not advertise GET; alternatively mount allowedMethods before the public middleware registers its catch-all.
